analysis:
NativeWorkerRuntime.swift (head 16, 37-45, plus dispatch cases 87-292) adds a Gemma4TensorParallelResidentRuntime owner. It is selected when family==.qwenDense, mode==.tensorParallel and Gemma4TensorParallelResidentRuntime.serves(runtimeModelID:) matches configuration.identity.modelID. The guard at head 41 requires no speculation, no assistant policy, equal [1,1] shares and a keyed dataPlane, and fails closed otherwise. This mirrors the GLM TP guard (head 62).

The owner receives prefixSSDKey, so the T-041 SSD prefix-cache tier extends to Gemma TP. The cache's own implementation, salt scoping and HMAC naming are not in this batch. Integration should verify that Gemma4TensorParallelResidentRuntime.load uses the existing keyed SSD tier and cacheSalt scoping. The model-ID match must also come from a coordinator-authored or qualified identity, not provider-chosen input (T-054/T-041).

JACCLOwnerBootstrap.requireConsumedIfInstalled still runs after load (head 80). releaseIdleMemory drops prefix entries under pressure (head 142). retiresCancelledLanes returns lanes>1 (head 245). Its cancel-ACK correctness (T-010) depends on the unseen Gemma runtime.

GemmaCheck.swift (new, 1-500) is a diagnostic tp-check CLI. Its sealed-bench mode uses QwenTensorParallelSealCodec.bench with unauthenticated ephemeral keys. The source explicitly labels this as cost measurement only and restricts it to tp mode. The allsum path installs a bench codec unconditionally (patch 475-500); that is still a diagnostic tool. Reports exclude hosts, addresses and paths. Input files are bounded (request under 1 MiB; outputCount and chunkSize capped). The tool is not a production path.

No regression identified. The concern for deeper review is that bench codecs must not be reachable from production worker code.
